title: Trial scorecard + micro-bench notes — Cameron
body:
Purpose: compact personal scorecard for small inference trials — capture p50/p95, cost impact, quick notes and next steps. Keeps me honest when iterating on cache/batching and quant configs.

Legend: p50/p95 in ms, tokens/s measured at steady-state, cost_est = estimated $ per 1k output tokens (rough) for this config.

---
Table (most recent at top):
Trial | Date | Model | Quant | Batch | Seq | p50_ms | p95_ms | tokens/s | cost_per_1k | notes
T-006 | 2026-02-18 | redwood-13b-v2 | int8 | 8 | 512 | 48 | 126 | 420 | 0.37 | KV-cache ON (prefill 64), occasional jitter when cold
T-005 | 2026-02-11 | redwood-13b-v2 | fp16 | 4 | 1024 | 92 | 220 | 190 | 0.85 | higher p95, no cache, useful baseline
T-004 | 2026-01-29 | llama-70b | int8 | 2 | 256 | 210 | 540 | 70 | 1.9 | heavy memory pressure, batch=2 ok for latency trials
T-003 | 2026-01-18 | redwood-7b | int4 | 16 | 256 | 22 | 58 | 780 | 0.12 | cheap and fast; quant artifacts minor on long tails
T-002 | 2025-12-05 | redwood-13b-v1 | int8 | 8 | 512 | 56 | 130 | 390 | 0.41 | kernel mismatch observed on one node (Investigate compiler flags)
T-001 | 2025-11-02 | redwood-13b-v1 | fp16 | 8 | 512 | 85 | 205 | 210 | 0.78 | initial baseline run, no caching, warm-up observed

---
Short observations (quick bullets):
- Best cost/latency tradeoff so far: redwood-7b + int4 for low-complexity prompts (T-003). Good for prototyping.
- For production chat with context ~1k tokens, redwood-13b + int8 + KV-cache seems promising (T-006). Need to reduce p95 jitter.
- fp16 runs consistently higher p95 for long sequences (T-005). Quantization helps but watch for hallucination tests.
- Tokens/s correlates strongly with batch size until memory becomes binding; track GPU mem utilization live next runs.

Unresolved questions / hypotheses to test:
- Why did T-002 show kernel mismatch warnings on node-5? Hypothesis: compiler flags/driver version mismatch; escalate to infra if reproduced.
- Can prefill size be increased from 64 to 128 without p95 regression? Quick A/B: T-006A (prefill 128) planned.
- Measure KV cache hit ratio per user session (not just global); may reveal uneven benefits.

Next short plan (todo list):
- [ ] Run T-006A (prefill=128) on redwood-13b-v2 int8, batch=8, record p95/p50/tokens/s (target window: 2026-02-25).
- [ ] Reproduce T-002 kernel warning on staging; collect dmesg + driver info, open INF follow-up if needed.
- [ ] Add simple quality check: sample 50 prompts and compute loss delta between fp16 vs int8 to detect regression.
- [ ] Add a small trace-level metric: per-request KV-cache-hit boolean (for batch experiments).

Notes to self and rough commands:
- To run local quick: ./tools/quick-bench --model redwood-13b-v2 --quant int8 --batch 8 --seq 512 --prefill 64 --out csv
- For cost est: assume $0.0009 per token-gen-op for 13b-int8 baseline and scale approx by tokens/s delta. Keep in spreadsheet.

References / links above: JIRA INF-3421 is the investigation ticket for kernel mismatch. PR 1234 is the change that added prefill control flags. Slack thread contains some early heap traces from Diego.

Quick mental log (end-of-day): happy with int8 baseline; need better observability on cache warmup; avoid fp16 on long-seq until we resolve p95 tail sources.

----
Scratch area (short snippets):
- idea: try hybrid prefill (short prefill warm, background prefill extended) to reduce cold-start p95.
- TODO: sensibility-check cost_per_1k formula in sheet: currently naive, add per-GPU-hours breakdown.
